A cold wind sweeps through Germany. Angela Merkel’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has been doing nothing but losing ground over the years. The people of Germany claim that the CDU is not longer conservative on any issues of value to the average citizen of Germany. But with the Christian Social Union of Bavaria having her back, she remains the most powerful woman in Germany, wielding more power, in theory, than Adolf Hitler had.

But parties rise to challenge Merkel and the CDU

From East Germany, the Alternative for Germany (AfD) stands, promising a return to traditional values and, more to the point, euroscepticism. Intellectuals make up most of their ranks, as well as growing numbers of disenfranchised German youths. As of yet, they do not have clout, only a few seats in the Bundestag

Across rural Germany, under the new leadership of the charismatic Gustav Steiner, the National Democratic Party of Germany (NPD) finds itself rising slowly in popularity. With a new message, the average farmer and small town citizen sees values in traditional, down-to-earth values Steiner promotes. While unlikely to win, their growing numbers presents a problem for Germany and her future. Or perhaps worse yet, they might win enough seats to be a deciding factor in future coalitions. Steiner will no doubt become a problem as times goes on. As of yet, they have no seats in the Bundestag, but one in the European Parliament

Freie Wähler, free voters, promises direct democracy, populism, and a reform to Germany in total. They grow in numbers too. Though central in policies, they represent a total shake up of Germany’s political machine.

Then there’s the Christian Social Union of Bavaria. They are working with the CDU in a coalition government. They seem to have their doubts about Merkel as times goes on.

The last of the old parties still trying to reign in power is the Social Democratic Party of Germany, lead by the German Vice Chancellor, Sigmar Gabriel. But even they are losing numbers. Can they win this upcoming election and ensure Germany remains the social democracy it is?

Merkel does not know. Can Germany remain a regional power? Can she stay the economical and technological backbone of Europe? Can she remain unentangled with the wars slowly consuming the globe? Germany has a few months to do before elections are upon them.

She does not know.

Germany’s future remains uncertain.

So last week I bought SOMA and finished it in a couple of days. I previously played (and greatly enjoyed) Amnesia the Dark Descent and I was really surprised this game kinda sneaked up on me. Really I had no idea it was released until after a couple of days after the release, and before that I had never heard of it!

I enjoyed playing SOMA. The environment has a great atmosphere, both the indoor and outdoor areas. The story was interesting enough and did made me think a couple of times. Ultimately the story and my curiosity about what was going to happen really pushed me on.

When I compare it to Amnesia TDD I think it was less scary. I guess this is very personal but medieval castles just feel more scary to me. Another factor which might have made it less scary is the fact I played Amnesia twice and also finished several user mods. After a while you get kind of immune to the scare moments. You intuitively feel when something is going to happen and know better to deal with it maybe.

One thing I enjoyed more than TDD was the interactivity with other characters in the world. In TDD most conversations are flash backs where as SOMA has a kind of side-kick character guiding you through the game. I enjoyed it but I believe it may also factor into making the game less scary as you will feel less alone.

What are your experiences/opinions about SOMA?

I really enjoyed my playthrough of SOMA. Unlike you, I had it easier to adjust to a sci-fi setting than the medieval castle. Being underwater and everything falling apart are not a good combination. The interesting topics about consciousness were really heavy at some points. The ending kept me up at night.

The monsters weren't really that scary but the atmosphere made up for it. The game had very little jump scares which I found refreshing.
